## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
The smallest measured point, N=4000 (working set 288 KB, already past the L1d spill at N≈910 but within L2), shows the highest cost: 11.241 ns/p at q=0.01. Cost FALLS as N grows to 65000 (7.831 ns/p), crossing the L2→DRAM spill at N≈58254 with no knee — pure overhead amortization. From 65000 through 4M the curve is FLAT (7.823–8.116 ns/p at q=0.01), confirming no cache-spill penalty in DRAM. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the N-curve: the flat region sits at ~7.8 ns/p for q=0.01, ~8.6 ns/p for q=0.05, and ~11.8–12.3 ns/p for q=0.25, a roughly 50% overhead at high churn applied uniformly across all N.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 9.2 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 36% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. At q=0.05 the peak falls to 8.35 GB/s (33%), and at q=0.25 to 6.9 GB/s (27%). The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: even at the largest N where DRAM streaming should dominate, it never exceeds 36% of ceiling, and the flat ns/p from 65K to 4M shows the bottleneck is per-particle compute cost, not memory throughput. The transition with death rate is gradual — each increase in q raises the floor proportionally, consistent with branchy respawn logic adding fixed per-particle overhead rather than a bandwidth penalty.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize at all: the histogram shows zero vector-suffixed instructions. All floating-point work is scalar — `ldp s5, s6`, `fmul s5`, `fadd s5`, `fsub s5`, `fcvtzs` — processing one particle at a time. The scatter into the output buffer is byte-granular and fully scalar: `ldrb w2, [x1]`, `add w2, w2, w12`, `cmp w2, #0xff`, `csel w2, w2, w11, lo`, `strb w2, [x1]`, repeated for three color components plus a `strb w11` for alpha. The 20 `csel` and 6 `ccmp` instructions reflect per-particle bounds-checking and clamping that serialize the loop body. This scalar byte-store scatter explains why bandwidth stalls at 36% of ceiling — the `strb` writes cannot coalesce into cache-line-sized stores, and the branch-heavy control flow (`tbnz`, `b.ge`, `b.lo`, `cbz`) prevents any SIMD amortization.

## Verdict
Refuted — the compiler produced zero vector instructions, and peak bandwidth never exceeds 9.2 GB/s (36% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, N=262000. The scalar byte-granular scatter (`ldrb`/`add`/`csel`/`strb` per component) and 20 `csel`-driven bounds checks make auto-vectorization impossible, and the flat 7.8 ns/p floor in DRAM confirms the bottleneck is per-particle overhead, not streaming bandwidth. At q=0.25 the floor rises to 11.8 ns/p (6.1 GB/s, 24% of ceiling), further widening the gap.
